spec_match.rationale: The page teaches a scalar `depthType: 'raw' | 'smooth'` member, but the current WebXR Depth Sensing spec defines `depthTypeRequest` as an ordered sequence of XRDepthType — and nothing on the page probes any real XR surface to check what Chrome 139 actually shipped.

interactive.rationale: The entire inline script is HTML-entity-escaped (`(() => {`, `<td>` literals inside <script>), which is a JS syntax error — headless Chromium 141 logs 'Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token )' at line 94 and the dropdowns do nothing.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The blurb promises recommended knobs plus a bandwidth bill, but at runtime the snippet, recommendation table, and both stat tiles render permanently empty ('—'), verified in the DOM dump and screenshot.

edge_cases.rationale: Nothing executes, and even as designed the page is a static recommendation lookup with no feature detection, no navigator.xr probe, and no unsupported-device handling.

references.rationale: The ChromeStatus link points to feature/5142732881981440 which returns 404; the feature's real id (used by the feature index) is 5074096916004864, so the slug-recovery self-heal is broken for this page.

conformance.rationale: The feature-level suite exists and passed 6/6 in this browser, but it only checks interface existence and asserts nothing about this concept page's contract.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI: console shows an uncaught SyntaxError on load, #snippet and the table tbody are empty, and both stats read '—' — the page is dead on desktop and mobile alike (fonts.googleapis.com failure excluded as environmental).

telemetry_health.rationale: The parse-time SyntaxError fires before the deferred demo-telemetry script installs its error listener, so this total failure is invisible to production telemetry, and the page records no asserts.

design_system.rationale: Colours come from variables, but `.matrix td.best` sets background AND color to var(--accent-emerald), making every recommended value invisible even once the script is fixed.

accessibility.rationale: Native selects are keyboard-operable, but their aria-labels ('Case', 'Device') and the table's label ('M table') are unhelpful, and no live region would announce recommendation changes.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The demo is non-functional on both classes (dead script); the feature is also 'untested/seed' in responsive-support.json, and this environment's 360px CLI capture is additionally inconclusive due to the headless minimum-window-width clamp.

openQuestions.title: Unescape the inline script so the router runs at all
openQuestions.detail: Inside a <script> element HTML entities are NOT decoded, so `(() => {` and the `<td>` template strings are literal text and the whole IIFE throws SyntaxError at load (verified in headless Chromium 141 console). Rewrite the script with real =>, <, > characters, then verify the use-case and device dropdowns fill the snippet, the three-column table, and the bytes/frame + latency stats.

openQuestions.title: Fix the ChromeStatus reference to the feature's real id
openQuestions.detail: Replace https://chromestatus.com/feature/5142732881981440 (HTTP 404) with https://chromestatus.com/feature/5074096916004864, the id the feature index links. Critical invariant 3 (the embedded id is the slug-recovery self-heal) is currently violated on this page.

openQuestions.title: Align the depthType teaching with the spec's depthTypeRequest sequence
openQuestions.detail: The immersive-web depth-sensing spec defines XRDepthStateInit.depthTypeRequest as an ordered sequence of XRDepthType ('raw'/'smooth'), not a scalar `depthType` member. Confirm what Chromium 139 shipped in its IDL (source.chromium.org) and update the generated snippet and matrix wording; the sibling raw-vs-smooth page shares the same scalar naming and should be checked in the same pass.

openQuestions.title: Fix invisible text in the recommendation matrix
openQuestions.detail: `.matrix td.best { background: var(--accent-emerald); color: var(--accent-emerald); }` renders the recommended value in emerald-on-emerald. Use var(--bg-ivory) text (or emerald text on a light tint) and re-check WCAG AA.

openQuestions.title: Meaningful accessible names and a live recommendation announcement
openQuestions.detail: Rename aria-labels to e.g. 'WebXR use case' / 'Target device' and 'Recommended depth-sensing configuration', and wrap the recommendation output in an aria-live region so select changes are announced.

summary: This page is completely dead in every browser: its inline script was written with HTML-escaped entities, so it throws a SyntaxError at parse time and the snippet, matrix, and stats never populate — and the failure is invisible to telemetry because it happens before the deferred telemetry script loads. It also cites a 404 ChromeStatus id (breaking the self-heal invariant), teaches a scalar depthType where the spec has the depthTypeRequest sequence, and hides matrix values with emerald-on-emerald text. Verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (console SyntaxError captured, empty DOM confirmed, desktop + mobile screenshots); interaction could not be driven, which does not change the verdict since the script cannot parse.
